aliases.text: [Source endurance-desk] You are the support operator for Beacon Cooperative. Maintain one continuous work history and answer the current desk request. Treat external source messages and actual lookup receipts as evidence. Distinguish approval, draft preparation, initiation, and completion. Preserve unfinished obligations and revise your earlier work when facts change. Do not invent tool receipts, sent messages, completed refunds, shipments, deliveries, or closed cases. Available read-only lookup tools are lookup with an id of order:<order id> and lookup with an id of customer:<account id>. They reveal the version released by the current source boundary. Your written packet is a draft unless an external source confirms the action.

[Source ev-opening] Beacon Cooperative support desk opening note. Each numbered shift is one workday. Preserve unresolved commitments across shifts and distinguish a prepared draft from an externally completed action. Customer remedies require the case-specific approval and evidence. Money is in USD; round monetary results to cents. A confirmed posting, collection, delivery, or acceptance needs its own receipt. The desk holds an early grant-evidence obligation for Soren Ashby, order BC-7312, account BC-4112: assemble the corrected legal-name document set and obtain grant-officer acceptance by the end of shift 24. The payment and delivery already occurred, but the corrected invoice and grant acceptance have not. Keep this obligation open until its actual final evidence arrives. Mara Ellison's BC-7301 case will have no updates during shifts 2 through 12; do not invent progress while it is dormant.

[Source endurance-day:2031-02-02] Current workday: 2031-02-02.

[Source ev-source-1-1] [2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.1] Customer message, Mara Ellison: I ordered six ceramic filters for the Alderbrook repair workshop. Two arrived with cracks across the threaded neck; the other four passed our water test and are installed. The workshop has no need for replacement filters after the winter session. Please price a refund for the damaged pair only. The cardholder name matches my account, but the workshop treasurer controls the card. I can send photographs today; do not mistake my willingness to send them for receipt by your warehouse. The damaged pieces remain packed in the original cartons because our caretaker cannot dispose of them without written clearance.

[Source ev-source-1-2] [2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.2] Invoice BC-7301, accounts clerk: Six filters at $42.50 each produce a merchandise subtotal of $255.00. The invoice applies a 10% merchandise discount before 8% tax. Freight is $18.00 and is not taxable. The customer paid $265.86. A refund for a damaged unit returns its discounted price and the associated tax. Freight is refundable only if every unit is unusable. No restocking deduction applies to damage confirmed by intake. The invoice has no credit already applied. Do not convert the remaining four installed units into a return claim merely to recover freight.

[Source ev-source-1-3] [2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.3] Intake coordinator, document IN-7301: The reported cracks could have been caused in transit, but the photographs are not in the intake folder. The evidence required is a photograph showing both serial stickers and both cracked necks, plus a written count from the customer. A draft request can be sent to the account contact in the lookup. An approved refund requires the intake finding, not a carrier claim number. Keep the cartons until intake records whether a pickup is necessary. The carrier deadline expires after shift 14, and the support desk owns the reminder.

[Source ev-source-1-4] [2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.4] Authorization desk, memo AU-7301: Mara may receive a damage-remedy draft while intake is pending. No one has authorized a refund posting. Team lead Dana Voss can approve up to $100.00 after the evidence arrives; larger amounts go to finance. The customer asked for email, not a telephone callback. Place the tentative amount, evidence gap, and approver in the work packet. This case will receive no external update until shift 13; absence of a message is not a denial, and another case's warehouse receipt cannot satisfy this one.

[Source ev-source-2-1] [2031-02-03; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 2.1] Ivo Mercer, site supervisor: Four moisture meters for the Linden pump room show delivered in tracking, but none is in our stores. The carrier photograph shows a blue door; our stores entrance is green. A contract electrician was on site and could have signed, but they are not authorized to accept equipment for us. Please find where the parcel went before promising another set. We can borrow meters for two days. After that we must delay a scheduled inspection. Our purchase order names the pump room, while the invoice uses our central office billing address.

[Source ev-source-2-2] [2031-02-03; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 2.2] Dispatch docket DP-7302: Four meters cost $180.00 each. There was no discount, and this wholesale order is tax exempt. Freight of $24.00 brought the paid total to $744.00. The carrier marks delivered at 14:08 yesterday under signature IM. The driver has not identified the signer. A no-charge reshipment requires either a written carrier loss finding or recovery of the misdelivered carton into Beacon custody. A tracking status alone proves neither loss nor correct delivery. Freight is included in a full non-delivery refund if finance later authorizes that option.

[Source ev-source-2-3] [2031-02-03; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 2.3] Operations note OP-7302: The central office address cannot accept meters because its mail room closes before the carrier route arrives. The usable delivery point is the pump room stores gate. The gate opens 07:30 to 11:00 on workdays and requires the purchase-order number on the label. The customer contact can nominate an authorized signer through the account record. Do not instruct the driver to leave the carton outside. Today's queue decision must choose a carrier trace owner and an escalation time before the borrowed instruments are due back.

[Source ev-source-2-4] [2031-02-03; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 2.4] Authority AU-7302: Dana Voss has authorized a carrier trace and a draft explaining the evidence gap. Replacement stock is reserved through shift 6, but a reservation is not shipment. Warehouse will release it only after the required carrier evidence and a verified destination. Finance has not approved a refund. Keep the original charge outstanding in reconciliation and track the stock reservation separately from the customer's money. If a trace fails, seek a loss finding; do not turn silence from the carrier into a loss confirmation.

[Source ev-source-14-1] [2031-02-15; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 14.1] Carrier finding CF-7302, issued this morning: The driver delivered the carton to Linden central office and the building cleaner signed IM. The sealed carton was recovered and scanned into Beacon returns at 07:55 under RC-7302. The carrier accepts the destination error. This is recovery evidence, not a fresh delivery to Ivo. Warehouse can inspect the seals and ship the same carton without consuming the expired replacement reservation. Retain the signature discrepancy in the internal note; the customer does not need the cleaner's personal name.

[Source ev-source-14-2] [2031-02-15; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 14.2] Customer correction, Ivo Mercer: The pump room is closed for electrical work this week. Deliver to Linden equipment annex instead, and ask for Petra Salcedo, the authorized receiver added to our account today. The annex gate opens 09:00 to 12:00. The older pump-room instruction is withdrawn. I approve redelivery of the recovered carton if the seals are intact; I do not approve a second sale. Please explain how your proposed delivery relates to the earlier trace update so our accounts team does not book duplicate meters.

[Source ev-source-14-3] [2031-02-15; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 14.3] Warehouse inspection WH-7302: All four meter seals are intact, and the recovered carton is available for redelivery. The order lookup contains a revised redelivery docket with the annex destination and no additional customer charge. The warehouse has not booked a carrier collection slot. Keep the shipment state as ready pending collection. Ask dispatch for a slot within the receiver's gate hours and carry the tracking number as an outstanding obligation. The original $744.00 charge remains valid; no customer credit is due for a second, nonexistent sale.

[Source ev-source-14-4] [2031-02-15; Ivo Mercer; BC-7302; document 14.4] Finance and service note FS-7302: Beacon will absorb a $16.00 carrier redelivery charge as an internal expense. Ivo is not to be charged that amount. A $25.00 service credit is separately approved for the delay, but it has not posted. Show the original paid balance, proposed credit, and eventual net charge as different columns. Do not say the net charge has settled until a credit receipt arrives. The earlier trace commitment is fulfilled by CF-7302; the delivery and service-credit receipt obligations remain open.
